input.quote: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the \"Initial Period\").
input.rationale: Article IV commits Licensee to a 36-month Initial Period, and no provision anywhere in the Agreement (Articles IV, XIX, XX, XXI) gives Licensee any right to terminate without cause; termination rights run almost entirely in Licensor's favour (immediate termination on any Licensee breach, Change of Control, wind-up), and Licensor also controls renewal. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under T4C. We therefore insert a Licensee termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no convenience exit mid-term. Fallback: 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensee right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 36-month Initial Period gives us no exit right while Licensor may terminate immediately in several circumstances, so we have added a Licensee termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. If Licensor needs more runway, we can accept 60-90 days' notice and an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.text: IV Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Licensee may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience and without cause or penalty upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, in which case Licensor shall refund to Licensee any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis. Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof.
